newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein stable in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein stable in quiet trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Friday, with sharp falls in Malaysia keeping buyers at bay, traders said.

They said palm olein was traded at 1,400 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but offers were also heard at 1,405-10 but found no takers. Crude palm oil was offered at 1,190 rupiah/kg in Medan, against last done 1,213 rupiah.

"Sellers tried to raise their offer prices after values kept their uptrend in Malaysia this morning from yesterday," one trader said. "But the sudden fall in Malaysian prices soon after dampened sentiment. Some raised prices but got no support.
The traders said the market shrugged off news that the state-run Joint Marketing Board (KPB) had reduced April exports by 50 percent because of poor production.

"We reduced exports by 50 percent to 20,000 tonnes in April," a KPB official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters. "The 20,000 tonne shortfall in April was carried over to May, when exports returned to the normal 40,000 tonnes."
"That means 50 percent of the exports in May will be carried over to June, and the same will happen in June through October when we expect the schedule to return to normal," he said.
"Delays by KPB are not unusual," one trader said. "Even domestic allocations are late at times."
The traders said they expected palm olein prices to weaken next week because of the declines in Malaysia coupled with limited buying interest.
